The largest backwards compatibility change is that the precision of scalars is now preserved consistently. Two examples are: np.float32(3) + 3. now returns a float32 when it previously returned a float64. np.array(, dtype=np.float32) + np.float64(3) will now return a float64 array. (The higher precision of the scalar is not ignored.) For floating point values, this can lead to lower precision results when working with scalars. For integers, errors or overflows are possible.
